text:
Ivy: Customer request came in: they want an SLA-backed 'burst fallback' option for reserved pools — i.e., when burst exceeds commit, automatically route to a pre-approved fallback but with SLA guarantees about max lat/delta and clear billing. Need product + infra feasibility + launch criteria.

Diego: Feels doable. We should offer two SLA tiers:
- soft-fallback: auto-route, notify, billed at hosted rates. No SLA on latency but SLA on availability of fallback routing.
- hard-fallback (premium): auto-route and honor reserved pricing for fallback traffic OR provide credit; require contract addendum + buffer commitments.

Rina: Ops notes: we must avoid masking overloaded pools. Circuit-breaker semantics: only allow fallback after 3m sustained oversubscribe and progressive ramp (25% -> 75% -> 100) with health checks. Alerts when fallback engages and when fallback crosses error or latency thresholds.

Hiro: Implementation pieces:
- routing rule schema: fallback_policy {threshold_tokens_per_min, window_mins, models:list, billing_behavior}
- metrics emitted: fallback_engaged{pool,tenant,model}, fallback_ramp_phase, fallback_cost_delta
- control-plane UI + webhook event for customer notifications
- feature-flagged rollout per-tenant
Will need ~2 sprints for end-to-end (routing + billing + telemetry).

Clara: Commercials: customers expect transparency: console banner + webhook + daily reconciliation. For hard-fallback to keep reserved rate while using shared infra, sales needs a credit model and finance approval. Most customers will accept hosted-rate billing for fallback if notified.

fin-bot: finance: created ticket FIN-411 to evaluate fallback-credit policy and margin impact.

Ivy: Launch gating checklist proposal:
1) routing config + API documented and testable in staging
2) telemetry: fallback_engaged + cost_delta emitted and dashboards created
3) alerts & runbook: SRE agrees on thresholds + rollback commands
4) billing export: fallback_usage events in billing stream + reconciliation job in BQ
5) pilot: one customer + 72h canary with synthetic long-context traffic
6) legal/sales sign-off for any reserved-rate exceptions

Rina: Runbook quick snippet for rollback:
```
# pause fallback for pool
POST /api/pools/<id>/config {"fallback_enabled":false}
```

Diego: For rollout plan I'd like to phase: internal canary (48h) -> pilot customer (72h) -> opt-in beta. I'll own the rollout epic.

Ivy: Prioritization ask: this is customer-driven but narrow set of customers. Recommend medium priority in roadmap with pilot focus. If finance okays credits, bump to high for next sprint.

Clara: I'll surface to field: ask customers if hosted-rate fallback is acceptable or they need reserved-rate guarantees. Collect responses by EOD Wed.

Ivy: Cool. Action items: Diego: routing spec + ETA (3d), Hiro: billing event + BQ mapping (2d), Rina: runbook and alert thresholds (2d), Clara: customer feedback (by Wed), FIN-411 owner to report back. Revisit Friday 9am. :thumbsup:
